mainTopic: אגדה from the אברהם–אבימלך story, and why permission to injure or damage does or does not exempt the one who does it
overview: This amud opens with the end of a run of אגדה tied to the משנה's story of אברהם and אבימלך. רבא learns from לוט that it pays to stay close to a wealthy man. רב חנן and רבי יצחק teach that someone who calls on Heaven against another person is punished first, and that even an ordinary person's curse can come true. רבי אבהו adds that it is better to be chased than to chase. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and asks why someone told 'blind my eye, on condition you are exempt' still pays, while damage to property done with permission is exempt. Three reasons are given: harm to the family (רב ששת, רבי אושעיא), that no one forgives the loss of his major limbs (רבא), and that a 'yes' can really mean 'no' (רבי יוחנן). Next, a contradiction with a ברייתא about a שומר is settled by רבה: what matters is whether the item was handed over to guard it or to tear it. The amud ends with רב יוסף's ruling about a stolen charity purse, followed by the הדרן closing פרק החובל.

steps.title: Closing verse of the previous proof: an angel sent to guard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק that served as the source for an earlier folk saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Behold, I send an angel before you, to guard you on the way."
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a discussion that started on the previous page. The גמרא is finishing a proof by quoting this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבא was asking רבה בר מרי where various popular sayings come from. This פסוק completes one of those answers. It shows that a מלאך was sent to guard the Jewish people in place of הקב"ה Himself.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a new question here. This פסוק is the tail end of an answer that began earlier, before this section.

phrases.english: "Behold, I send an angel before you,
phrases.notes: שמות 23:20

phrases.english: to guard you on the way."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof begun before this section
steps.raayaObject: A popular saying discussed just before this section

steps.title: רבא asks for the source of 'Drag wood after a rich man'
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי which פסוק is the source for the saying that you should help a wealthy man even with small jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: Where does the thing people say come from: "Behind a property owner, drag wood"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for a פסוק that supports a common saying. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means you should attach yourself to a wealthy person, even by doing small chores like carrying firewood. You may end up gaining from his success. רבא wants to know where the תורה hints at this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this matter? (a request for a source)
An owner of property, a wealthy man

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי,
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari,
From where is this matter that people say:
Behind a property owner, drag wood?
phrases.notes: In other words, help a rich man even in a small way, because you may end up benefiting from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same series of 'where does this saying come from'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that supports the saying about helping a wealthy man

steps.title: The source: לוט became wealthy by going with אברם
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי answers from the פסוק that לוט, who traveled with אברם, also had flocks, herds and tents.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written, "And also לוט, who went with אברם, had flocks, cattle and tents."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers רבא's question with a פסוק about לוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "who went with Avram" show why לוט had all that wealth. Because he stuck close to אברם, he shared in אברם's blessing. That is the same idea as the saying: stay near a wealthy man and you will gain too.
steps.whatToRemember: Attaching yourself to a successful person can bring you blessing, as we see with לוט and אברם.

phrases.english: He said to him, as it is written:
"And also Lot, who went with Avram,
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:5

phrases.english: had flocks and cattle and tents."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בראשית 13:5: לוט gained wealth by going with אברם

steps.title: רב חנן: whoever hands his fellow's judgment to Heaven is punished first
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן teaches that someone who asks Heaven to judge another person is himself punished first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said: One who hands over judgment against his fellow to Heaven is punished first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב חנן. It is connected to the story of אברהם, which the משנה mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking Heaven to judge someone is risky. Heaven then looks closely at the person who asked too, and he gets punished before the one he complained about.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hands over judgment (to Heaven)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson about not rushing to call on Heaven against another person.

phrases.english: Rav Chanan said:
One who hands over judgment against his fellow,
phrases.notes: He means asking Heaven to judge the other person.

phrases.english: he is punished first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New teaching, linked to the אברהם story from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who calls on Heaven to judge another is punished first

steps.title: Proof from שרי: she called for judgment and died first
steps.stepSummary: שרי said 'my wrong is upon you' and asked הקב"ה to judge between her and אברם. Later the תורה tells us אברהם mourned שרה, which shows she died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And שרי said to אברם: My wrong is upon you." And it is written: "And אברהם came to eulogize שרה and to weep for her."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב חנן's teaching from two פסוקים about שרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, שרי asks הקב"ה to judge אברם. The second פסוק shows that שרה died before אברהם, since he mourned her. So the one who called for judgment was punished first.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Sarai said to Avram:
My wrong is upon you,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 16:5. The פסוק goes on: 'Let ה' judge between me and you.'

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Avraham came
to eulogize Sarah and to weep for her."
phrases.notes: בראשית 23:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב חנן's teaching
steps.raayaObject: רב חנן's teaching that one who hands over judgment is punished first

steps.title: Limit: only when a human court was available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב חנן's teaching to a case where the person could have gone to a court in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only where he has a court on earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב חנן's rule. It tells us exactly when the punishment applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a human court could have handled the matter, turning to Heaven instead is wrong, and the one who does it is punished first. If there is no human court that can help him, he may cry out to Heaven without this danger.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply (only when...), a limiting phrase

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean crying out to Heaven is always forbidden. The danger is only when a human court was available and he skipped it.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone who calls on Heaven to judge another person is punished first, but only when he could have gone to a human court.

phrases.english: And these words apply
where he has judgment on earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule taught in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment applies only when a human court was available

steps.title: רבי יצחק: woe to the one who cries out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that the one who cries out to Heaven is worse off than the one he cries out about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Woe to the one who cries out, more than to the one cried out against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching from רבי יצחק on the same theme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק makes the same point in stronger words. The complainer is in more danger than the person he complains about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Woe to the one who cries out
more than to the one cried out against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel teaching that strengthens רב חנן's point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who cries out to Heaven is at greater risk than the one he cries out about

steps.title: A ברייתא supports Rabbi Yitzchak
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that both the one crying out and the one cried out against are included in the פסוק, but the one who cries out is punished sooner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Both the one who cries out and the one cried out against are included in the meaning, but they hurry to punish the one who cries out more than the one cried out against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about crying out to הקב"ה warns of punishment, and the ברייתא says both people are covered by that warning. Yet Heaven acts faster against the one who cried out. This matches what happened with שרה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
Included in the meaning (of the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Both people are judged, but the one who cries out to Heaven is punished first.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
both the one who cries out and the one cried out against are included,
phrases.notes: Included in the פסוק about crying out to הקב"ה (שמות 22:22–23).

phrases.english: but they hurry to punish the one who cries out
more than the one cried out against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יצחק's teaching with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's teaching that the one who cries out is worse off

steps.title: Do not take an ordinary person's curse lightly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that even the curse of a regular person can come true, pointing to אבימלך's curse of שרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Never treat the curse of an ordinary person as unimportant. אבימלך cursed שרה, and the curse came true in her child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another lesson from רבי יצחק, taken from the same story of אבימלך, שרה and אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדיוט is a regular person, not a prophet or a great צדיק. Even so, his curse can have real power. רבי יצחק names the example now and proves it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse of an ordinary person
It came true in her offspring

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There should never be
the curse of an ordinary person light in your eyes.
For Avimelech cursed Sarah,
and it was fulfilled in her offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי קִלְלַת הֶדְיוֹט קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רבי יצחק, drawn from the same אברהם and אבימלך story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an ordinary person's curse can come true, so do not take it lightly.

steps.title: Proof: אבימלך's curse and יצחק's blindness
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כסות עינים' is read as a curse that שרה's children would have covered eyes, and it came true when יצחק's eyes grew dim.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says, 'It is a covering of the eyes for you.' אבימלך told her: Since you covered up the truth and did not tell me he is your husband, and you caused me this suffering, may you have children whose eyes are covered. It came true in her son, as it says: 'When יצחק was old, his eyes were too dim to see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי יצחק's teaching by reading אבימלך's words as a curse and showing that it came true in יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כסות עינים' are read as a play on words. שרה 'covered' (כיסית) the truth, so her children would have 'covered eyes'. יצחק's blindness in old age shows that the curse of a non-prophet came true.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes" –
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:16

phrases.english: He said to her: Since you concealed from me
and did not reveal that he is your husband,
and you caused me this suffering,
may it be God's will that you will have
children with covered eyes.
And it was fulfilled in her offspring – as it is written:
"And it was when Isaac was old,
and his eyes were too dim to see."
phrases.notes: בראשית 27:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוקים that prove רבי יצחק's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That an ordinary person's curse can come true
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 20:16 read as a curse, fulfilled in בראשית 27:1

steps.title: Be among the chased, not the chasers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that a person should always choose to be the one pursued rather than the pursuer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: A person should always be one of those who are chased, and not one of those who chase.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אבהו about choosing to be the victim rather than the attacker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the theme of the last steps: it is better to suffer harm than to cause it. The proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
A person should always be among the pursued,
and not among the pursuers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם מִן הַנִּרְדָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ethical teaching that continues the theme of how to act toward those who harm you.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is better to be the one pursued than the one pursuing.

steps.title: Proof from doves offered on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: תורים ובני יונה are the most chased birds, and they are the birds the תורה chose for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No birds are chased more than turtledoves and young pigeons, and the תורה made them fit to be brought on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי אבהו's teaching from the birds the תורה chose for קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other birds hunt doves and pigeons more than any other birds. Out of all birds, these are the only ones fit for a קרבן. So being the one chased brings closeness to הקב"ה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two lessons: never take an ordinary person's curse lightly (רבי יצחק), and it is better to be chased than to chase (רבי אבהו).

phrases.english: For there is no one more pursued among birds
than turtledoves and young pigeons,
and the verse made them fit for the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ נִרְדׇּף בָּעוֹפוֹת יוֹתֵר מִתּוֹרִים וּבְנֵי יוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבי אבהו's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That being pursued is better than pursuing
steps.raayaSupportSource: Only the most hunted birds are fit as קרבנות

steps.title: Why the difference between body and property?
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, רב אסי בר חמא asks רבא why someone told to injure a body is liable, while someone told to damage property is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'One who says, Blind my eye' and so on. רב אסי בר חמא asked רבא: What makes the first part different from the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks why its two cases end differently. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, a person says 'blind my eye' and promises not to make him pay, but the one who does it is still liable. In the סיפא, the person says 'tear my garment' with the same promise, and the one who does it is exempt. The question is what makes these two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

phrases.english: One who says "Blind my eye" etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי בַּר חָמָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Asi bar Chama said to Rava:
What is different about the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the injury to the body, where he is liable.

phrases.english: and what is different about the latter clause?
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the damage to property, where he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why permission with a promise of no payment works for property but not for bodily injury.

steps.title: People do not really give up payment for major body parts
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the רישא: a person does not truly forgive damage to his major limbs, so his promise of no payment is not taken seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא answered him: In the first part he is liable, because a person does not forgive damage to his major limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer by explaining why the attacker is liable in the case of bodily injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone says 'blind my eye and you won't have to pay', we assume he did not really mean to give up payment. No one truly waives payment for losing an eye, hand or foot. In the next step רב אסי בר חמא challenges this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Major limbs, such as eyes, hands and feet

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the permission was never given. He is saying we assume the person did not truly mean to give up his payment.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The first clause – because a person does not forgo
payment for his major limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא – לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מוֹחֵל עַל רָאשֵׁי אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of רב אסי בר חמא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For bodily injury we assume the victim did not truly waive payment, since no one forgives damage to major limbs.

steps.title: Does a person forgive his own pain? A ברייתא says yes
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר חמא attacks רבא's explanation. A ברייתא says that if someone says 'hit me, wound me, on condition that you are exempt', the hitter is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does a person really forgive his own pain? It was taught in a ברייתא: 'Hit me, wound me, on condition that you are exempt.' He is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי בר חמא pushes back on רבא's answer. He brings a ברייתא where a person does forgive an injury to his body, and the hitter is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a person does not really mean it when he forgives an injury to his body. But the ברייתא shows that a person can forgive a bodily injury like hitting or wounding. So 'people don't forgive harm to their bodies' seems to be wrong, and רבא's reason for the משנה is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that you are exempt (from paying)

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'Does a person forgive his pain?!' is said with surprise, meaning 'surely nobody really wants to give up payment for his pain either!' Yet the ברייתא rules that the hitter is exempt. So by רבא's logic the ברייתא should have made him pay, and that is the difficulty.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי אָדָם מוֹחֵל עַל צַעֲרוֹ?!
phrases.english: He said to him: And does a person forgive his pain?!
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי בר חמא pushing back on רבא's answer from Step 14.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Hit me, wound me,
on condition that you are exempt' — he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that a person does not truly forgive harm to his body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that a person does forgive hitting and wounding, and the hitter is exempt. So bodily harm can be forgiven, and רבא's reason seems to fail.

steps.title: רבא is silent and asks if רב אסי has heard an answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא has no answer to the challenge. He falls silent, then asks רב אסי whether he has heard anything about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. He said: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא cannot answer the challenge, so he goes quiet. Then he asks רב אסי if he knows an answer, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's silence shows the challenge was strong and his own reason could not defend itself here. Instead of guessing, he asks for a received teaching. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: רבא is the one who goes quiet. He has no answer to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said: Have you heard anything about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא cannot answer the challenge and asks for a received teaching
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב אסי knows a teaching that explains the משנה's first case without this problem

steps.title: רב ששת: the reason is harm to the family name
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רב ששת: the person is liable in the משנה's first case because of פגם משפחה, a flaw that harms the family.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said: Because of a family flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a new reason for the משנה's first case. Losing a limb harms the whole family's standing, not just the injured person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason solves the challenge. The injured person can forgive his own pain, which is why the ברייתא about hitting and wounding says exempt. But blinding an eye or cutting off a hand also brings a flaw to his family, and he cannot give that up for them.

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw or shame to the family

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer separates the two kinds of injury. Ordinary wounds can be forgiven, but losing a limb affects others, so it cannot be forgiven by one person alone.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: He said to him, this is what רב ששת said:
Because of a family flaw.
phrases.notes: This explains why the משנה's case of blinding or cutting off a limb is still liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question and resolves the challenge with a different reason
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The liability in the משנה's first case is because losing a limb harms the family, which the injured person cannot forgive on their behalf. His own pain he can forgive.

steps.title: The dispute is recorded: רבי אושעיא versus רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records a formal disagreement. רבי אושעיא gives the family-flaw reason, while רבא keeps his reason that a person does not forgive harm to his major limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי אושעיא says: Because of a family flaw. רבא says: Because a person does not forgive the harm to his major limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lays out two opinions side by side on why the משנה's first case is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא holds the same reason as רב ששת: harm to the family. רבא stays with his own reason, that a person does not truly forgive losing his limbs. So רבא did not drop his view after the challenge; it is recorded as a real opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Major limbs, the 'heads' of the limbs (like eye or hand)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבא fell silent in Step 16 when he was challenged, the גמרא here still records his reason as a real opinion next to רבי אושעיא's.

phrases.english: It was stated, רבי אושעיא says:
Because of a family flaw.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מוֹחֵל
phrases.english: רבא says: Because a person does not forgive
the harm to his major limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally records the two reasons just discussed as a dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא: liable because of family flaw. רבא: liable because a person does not forgive harm to his major limbs.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: sometimes 'yes' means 'no'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a third approach. Sometimes a 'yes' is really a 'no', and sometimes a 'no' is really a 'yes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: There is a 'yes' that is like a 'no', and there is a 'no' that is like a 'yes'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a third way to look at the משנה's case. A person's words do not always show what he really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the person said 'on condition that you are exempt', which sounds like a 'yes' to giving up payment. רבי יוחנן's rule suggests such a 'yes' may not be sincere, so it does not count as real forgiveness. His rule also works the other way: a 'no' can sometimes be treated as a 'yes'.
steps.whatToRemember: Three reasons for why blinding or cutting off a limb 'on condition you are exempt' is still liable: harm to the family (רב ששת, רבי אושעיא), a person does not forgive his major limbs (רבא), and a 'yes' that is really a 'no' (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יֵשׁ ״הֵן״ שֶׁהוּא כְּ״לָאו״,
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן says: There is a 'yes' that is like a 'no',
and there is a 'no' that is like a 'yes'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, separate explanation alongside the two in the recorded dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's spoken 'yes' can mean 'no' (and a 'no' can mean 'yes'), so his agreement to exempt the injurer may not be real.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs רבי יוחנן's yes-means-no idea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that when someone says 'hit me, wound me', a 'yes' about exempting the hitter really means 'no.' When someone says 'tear my garment', a 'no' really means 'yes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: Someone says 'Hit me, wound me.' The other asks, 'On condition that I am exempt?' He answers 'Yes.' This is a 'yes' that is like a 'no.' Someone says 'Tear my garment.' The other asks, 'On condition that I am exempt?' He answers 'No.' This is a 'no' that is like a 'yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports what רבי יוחנן just said in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About his body, the person's 'yes' is said with surprise, meaning 'Yes?! You think I would let you off?' So the hitter must pay. About his garment, his 'no' means 'No, of course I won't make you pay; why else would I ask you to tear it?' So the one who tears is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
On condition that I am exempt from paying

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the words 'yes' and 'no' are read by their tone and the situation. People do not really forgive harm to their body, but they do give up their money when they ask for it to be ruined.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the 'yes' and the 'no' as plain answers. Each one is said as a surprised question, so it means the opposite of the bare word.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
"Hit me, wound me,"
"On condition that I am exempt?"
phrases.notes: This is the hitter asking. He wants to know if he'll be free from paying.

phrases.english: and he said to him "Yes"
phrases.notes: Picture him saying it with surprise: "Yes?! You really think I'd let you off?"

phrases.english: here there is a "yes" that is like a "no."
"Tear my garment,"
"On condition that I am exempt?"
and he said to him: "No"
here is a "no" that is like a "yes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's approach from Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that a 'yes' can mean 'no' and a 'no' can mean 'yes'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about 'hit me, wound me' and 'tear my garment' with the condition of being exempt

steps.title: The משנה's 'break my jug' clashes with the guardian ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that someone told 'break my jug, tear my garment' is liable. But a ברייתא learns from the פסוקים about guardians that a person given an item to destroy or tear is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Break my jug,' 'Tear my garment': he is liable. But a ברייתא teaches the opposite: the פסוק says 'to guard', and not to destroy; 'to guard', and not to tear; 'to guard', and not to give out to the poor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new line of the משנה. It points out that the משנה and a ברייתא about a שומר seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the damager pay even though the owner told him to break or tear the item. The ברייתא reads the word 'לשמור' in the פסוק to say a guardian only pays when the item was given to him to guard. If he was given it to tear, he does not pay, even without any condition about being exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction (between two sources)
To guard; the word in the פסוק about a שומר
To give out to the poor

phrases.english: "Break my jug," "Tear my garment": he is liable.
And a contradiction was raised:
"To guard", and not to destroy,
"To guard", and not to tear,
"To guard", and not to give out to the poor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of bodily harm and begins a new discussion about the משנה's ruling on damaging property with permission.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who breaks a jug or tears a garment at the owner's request is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts a guardian who was given an item to tear or destroy, without any condition of exemption. This seems to directly contradict the משנה's ruling that he pays.

steps.title: רב הונא: it depends whether the item was in his hands
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the two sources deal with different cases. One is about an item that came into the damager's hands, and the other is about an item that did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is not difficult. This one is where it came into his hands; that one is where it did not come into his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction by splitting the two sources into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the item had already come into his hands as a guardian, so he was responsible for it before the owner told him to tear it. Because of that, he still pays. In the ברייתא, the item never came into his care. He just tore it, so he does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
Where it came into his hands (his care)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It is not difficult;
this is where it came into his hands,
phrases.notes: "This" means our משנה, where he pays.

phrases.english: that is where it did not come into his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source deals with a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to rule differently about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an item already in his care, so he pays. The ברייתא is about an item that never came into his care, so he is exempt.

steps.title: רבה: 'to guard' means it was in his hands
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects to רב הונא's answer. The word 'לשמור' in the ברייתא itself shows that the item did come into the guardian's hands, and yet the ברייתא exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: 'To guard' implies that it came into his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב הונא's answer from Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the ברייתא is about an item that never came into his hands. But the ברייתא is built on the word 'לשמור', which only fits a guardian who already holds the item. So the ברייתא really is about an item in his hands, and it still exempts him. That brings the contradiction back.

keyTerms.meaning: It implies; the plain meaning shows

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
"To guard" implies that it came into his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the ברייתא deals with an item that did not come into his hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own word 'לשמור' describes a guardian who already holds the item. So רב הונא cannot place the ברייתא in a case where it never reached his hands, and the contradiction returns.

steps.title: רבה's answer: given to guard versus given to tear
steps.stepSummary: רבה agrees that in both sources the item came into the person's hands. The difference is the reason he received it: in one case to guard it, in the other case to tear it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: in both sources the item came into his hands, and there is no contradiction. One is where it came to him to be guarded. The other is where it came to him to be torn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה dropped רב הונא's answer in the last step, and now he gives his own way to settle the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא split the cases by whether the item came into his hands. רבה showed that both did. So רבה splits them by the purpose of the handover instead. The ברייתא's word 'לשמור' (to guard) leaves out an item given to be torn. That is why the ברייתא exempts the person who received it in order to tear it.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, meaning both sources
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
As something to guard (given for safekeeping)
As something to tear (given in order to be torn)

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
This and that are where it came into his hands,
and it is not difficult;
this is where it came into his hands as something to guard,
that is where it came into his hands as something to tear.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case. The word 'לשמור' leaves it out, so he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: הָא וְהָא דַּאֲתָא לִידֵיהּ, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה replaces רב הונא's answer, which he knocked down in Step 23, with a new distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by the purpose for which the item was handed over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the sources differ on whether the item came into his hands at all, which was רב הונא's answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both came into his hands. The משנה is about an item given to guard. The ברייתא, which exempts, is about an item given to be torn, which 'לשמור' leaves out.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule: what matters is why the item was handed over, to guard or to tear, and not just whether it reached the person's hands.

steps.title: The stolen charity purse in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: A purse of charity money came to פומבדיתא. רב יוסף gave it to a man to keep, the man was careless, and thieves stole it. רב יוסף ruled that the man must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain purse of charity money came to פומבדיתא. רב יוסף deposited it with a certain man. He was careless with it, and thieves came and stole it. רב יוסף held him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story about a guardian of charity money and gives רב יוסף's ruling. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was a guardian, and a guardian who is careless usually has to pay for theft. The new question is whether the same is true when the money is charity, meant for the poor. רב יוסף said yes, he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: He deposited it (gave it to be watched)
He held him liable (ruled that he must pay)

phrases.english: A certain purse of charity
that came to Pumbedita,

phrases.aramaic: אַפְקְדַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף גַּבֵּי הָהוּא גַּבְרָא.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef deposited it with a certain man.
He was negligent with it,
thieves came and stole it.
Rav Yosef held him liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It moves to a story that uses the same ברייתא about the word 'לשמור'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A careless guardian of charity money who let it get stolen must pay.

steps.title: אביי: the verse says to guard, not to hand out to the poor
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף from a ברייתא. The word 'לשמור' leaves out money given to be handed out to the poor, so the guardian should not be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'To guard', and not to hand out to the poor!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's ruling by quoting a ברייתא that seems to exempt someone holding money meant for the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of reading that רבה just used. 'לשמור' only covers items handed over to be guarded. Money given to be handed out to the poor seems to fall outside that, so the guardian rules would not apply and he should not have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: To guard; a word from the פסוק about guardians
To hand out to the poor

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
But wasn't it taught:
"To guard", and not to distribute to the poor!
phrases.notes: The word לשמור comes from שמות 22:6, the פסוק about a guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that the guardian of the charity purse must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא reads 'לשמור' as leaving out money given to be handed out to the poor. So this guardian should be exempt.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the poor of פומבדיתא had fixed amounts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the poor of פומבדיתא each had a fixed amount set for them. So this money was really 'to guard', and the guardian must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The poor of פומבדיתא have a fixed amount set for them, so this is 'to guard'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his ruling by explaining that this charity money does not fit the case the ברייתא leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא leaves out money given to be handed out to the poor. In פומבדיתא, though, each poor person's share was already fixed. So the money was being held for set people, and that counts as 'לשמור', to guard. That is why the careless guardian is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fixed for them; each has a set amount

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי.

phrases.english: the poor of Pumbedita have a fixed amount set for them,
and so it is "to guard".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַנְיֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מִיקָּץ קִיץ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: showing this case is different from the one the ברייתא leaves out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought that all charity money meant for the poor falls outside 'לשמור'.
steps.terutzMaskana: When each poor person's share is already fixed, the money is being guarded for them. That counts as 'לשמור', so the careless guardian is liable.
steps.whatToRemember: Charity money is left out of the guardian rules only when it is just for handing out. If the poor already have fixed shares, it counts as 'to guard', and a careless guardian must pay.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing פרק החובל
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of פרק החובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק החובל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the standard closing line that marks the end of the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the chapter about someone who wounds another, פרק החובל, is finished, and it shows our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said at the end of a chapter
One who wounds; the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaChovel

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last story.
